subject: Post-demo: Hosted evaluation — deployment path questions and SLO probes
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara@finpath.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-07-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap and a couple hosted evaluation clarifications

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the candid run-through of FinPath's production constraints. Quick recap and two asks so we can laser-focus the hosted evaluation:

Recap:
- Use case: real-time customer support summarization + risk-detection microservice.
- Expected peak traffic: ~120 rps bursts, baseline 8-12 rps.
- Latency target: 180–250ms p50 for single-turn summaries.
- Data residency: US-only; no on-prem requirement for the pilot.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm whether FinPath prefers an isolated Dedicated pool for the pilot, or if we should proceed on Hosted API sandbox endpoints first? From our side Hosted works for the pilot if you can accept shared-hosted sandbox endpoints with data controls — Dedicated would be next step once throughput or SLA needs are firm.
2) You've mentioned a security questionnaire — please send the list. I attached a short one-pager with common items (finpath_security_qs.pdf) and the recording of today's demo (demo_recording_20260706.mp4).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- If Hosted sandbox: we provision two sandbox endpoints (low-latency gen / reranker) and a 30k token sandbox credit slice; set rate limits to match your burst profile and enable prefix/KV cache for common prompts.
- If Dedicated: we surface an early capacity estimate and a timeline (usually 2–4 weeks for reserved capacity onboarding).

Can you loop in whoever owns infra for a quick 30-min call tomorrow so we can confirm network egress, IP allowlists, and rate-floor needs? I copied Ben and Kim on ops details below.

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your constraints.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- For the pilot we'd prefer to start on Hosted sandbox if it can meet latency targets; we want to avoid procurement overhead. Dedicated may be necessary if shared-hosted causes jitter.
- Burst profile: the 120 rps peaks are short (1–2 minute spikes) tied to batch batch uploads; steady-state is ~10 rps.
- Security questionnaire: attached internally; we will share the SOC-2 and application security checklist by EOD.
- Network: we can allowlist IPs but have a VPC egress constraint. Does hosted sandbox support TLS mutual auth or IP allowlist for the trial?

Can we do a 30-min technical sync today at 3pm PT? DevOps (infra@finpath.com) will be on.

Sara Gomez
Head of Product
FinPath
sara@finpath.com

Team — forwarding FinPath's reply. Key asks we should be ready to answer on the 3pm sync:

- Hosted sandbox feasibility for 180–250ms p50 on their baseline/burst profile; they prefer to start on Hosted and only move to Dedicated if jitter breaks their SLAs.
- IP allowlist / TLS mutual auth support for sandbox endpoints (they have VPC egress constraints).
- Short burst handling: 120 rps spikes for 1–2 minutes — need guidance on rate limiting, autoscaling, and recommended per-endpoint concurrency.

Proposed internal ownership:
- Ben: lead the 3pm call, align on sandbox endpoint provisioning and quota plan.
- Kim: confirm network-level constraints and whether hosted sandbox can support IP allowlist or mTLS, or whether we should recommend a Dedicated preview with VPC.
- Monica: be ready with CS plan and success criteria (latency SLOs, error budgets, monitoring hooks).

I suggested we propose a sandbox plan: two endpoints, initial ratecaps (burst 150 rps, sustained 15 rps per endpoint), and prefix/KV caching for common prompts. Ben, can you draft a short pilot runbook and a checklist for the call? I'll share the demo recording and their security note.

Thanks,
Jasmine

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap and a couple hosted evaluation clarifications — FinPath asks

All — thanks for the heads up. Draft plan below for the 3pm sync and a checklist I can share with FinPath immediately.

Draft pilot plan (Hosted sandbox):
- Provision two sandbox endpoints: /v1/hosted-gen (low latency) and /v1/hosted-rerank.
- Initial quotas: sustained 15 rps per endpoint, burst ceiling 150 rps with token-based throttling; pre-warm strategy to reduce cold-starts.
- Autoscale policy: scale based on request concurrency and queue depth with fast-start for short spikes (1–2 min). We'll recommend a soft throttling window to keep p50 within 250ms.
- Networking: Hosted sandbox cannot do customer-managed VPC or HSM keys. For IP allowlist we can provide static egress IPs for their region or mTLS at the edge — Kim, need confirmation which of those we can promise for sandbox.
- Observability: Provide a shared dashboard (token-level latency/cost), error-rate alerts, and a webhook for their incident channel.
- Success criteria: p50 < 250ms for 95% of steady-state traffic and < 300ms under burst for 90% of requests; error rate < 0.5%.

Checklist for the 3pm call to confirm with FinPath:
1) Which endpoints to provision and sample payloads.
2) Exact burst profile and time-of-day for spikes.
3) IP allowlist vs mTLS preference.
4) Any payload residency/content filtering needs (PII patterns).
5) Access: who needs sandbox keys and admin access to the dashboard.

I'll prepare a 1-page pilot runbook and share it in chat before the call. Kim — after the call, if they need strict network isolation we should escalate to a Dedicated preview and provide an estimate for reserved capacity.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
